references.text: Moses gives further instructions on gathering manna, especially before the Sabbath, expanding on the prohibition against saving any for the next day.
Shows the consequence of disobeying Moses' command—the manna became infested with maggots and began to rot.
The saying about not worrying about tomorrow reflects trust in God's daily provision, as seen with the manna.
Jesus' prayer for 'our daily bread' connects to the daily miracle of manna and trust in God's daily care.
Jesus teaches his disciples not to worry about tomorrow, reflecting the principle of daily trust in God from the manna story.
Jesus refers to the manna that their ancestors ate in the wilderness and presents himself as the true bread from heaven.
A direct parallel in the instruction not to keep anything until the next morning, emphasizing total dependence on God's daily provision and sanctification.
